title: What a US-China AI Safety Channel Needs
text:
What a US-China AI Safety Channel Needs

Project Syndicate

Andrew Harnick/Getty Images

The following is an excerpt from an op-ed published in Project Syndicate on October 28, 2026, written by Lizzi C. Lee, Fellow on Chinese Economy at ASPI's Center for China Analysis, and Simon Hedlin, an AI policy researcher.The most concrete outcome from last month’s summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping was an apparent agreement to set up a US-China AI incident-reporting channel. But even if either government proves willing to use this direct line or start sending data across the Pacific, they must first address a more pressing issue: US and Chinese frontier AI companies currently do not provide the information they would need.In the US, no federal statute or regulation specifically requires AI companies to report safety incidents and dangerous capabilities to the government. Although some states have passed incident-reporting laws, federal legislation—such as the AI Incident Reporting Act and the FRONTIER Act—has stalled in Congress. The industry is still largely regulating itself.Read the full op-ed here.
